extracted.intended_audience: general CNN readership; people following international news, media accountability, and U.S. military affairs
extracted.subtask_description: A CNN news article recounting Newsweek's backing away from a report that U.S. interrogators desecrated copies of the Quran, the resulting riots, the journalistic sourcing and verification issues, and subsequent procedural changes at Guantanamo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic sourcing and pre-publication comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publishing the account the magazine approached two Pentagon officials for comment. One declined and the other challenged a different aspect of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek comment from relevant official sources prior to publication; attempt multiple avenues of comment and record responses. Treat an official's decline to comment or challenge as material that should temper certainty and trigger further verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on named/trusted sources and need for corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Isikoff called a longtime reliable source, a senior U.S. government official, who told him investigators' report would include details (including mention of flushing the Quran down a toilet). Later the source said he could no longer be sure those concerns had surfaced in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on a single 'longtime reliable' source for explosive allegations; corroborate with documentary evidence or independent witnesses. Re-check memory-based claims against primary reports before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative confirmation standard (military investigators)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pentagon said it was unable to corroborate any case in which interrogators defiled the Muslim holy book; investigators had to confirm log entries and physical evidence before concluding an incident occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should seek corroborating logs, reports, or eyewitness accounts and avoid confirming incidents based on unverified secondhand reports. Confirmatory standards include log entries and direct evidence rather than hearsay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability, corrections and editorial review after errors
rubrics_metrics.description: "We regret that we got any part of our story wrong..." Newsweek published an assessment asking, 'How did Newsweek get its facts wrong? And how did the story feed into serious international unrest?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting errors occur that have public harm, publish clear apologies and independent assessments of coverage; explain what went wrong and how similar errors will be prevented. Extend sympathies to victims where coverage contributed to unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of local legal and cultural consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: "Desecrating the Quran is a death-penalty offense" in Afghanistan and neighboring Pakistan, a fact cited to explain the severity of local reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and analysts should factor in local legal penalties and cultural sensitivities when reporting allegations, because factual claims can have disproportionate consequences in certain jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of allegations as potential propaganda or tactical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. military officials said such claims are 'standard terrorist tactics' and cited al Qaeda training encouraging allegations against the infidels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether explosive allegations might be used tactically by adversaries or insurgents; cross-check against known misinformation/propaganda patterns and weigh that possibility in reporting and investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/procedural safeguards for handling religious texts in detention settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Camp commanders established stronger procedures when searching near a Quran — including encasing a book in a surgical mask during searches and a rule that allows only Muslim troops, interrogators or chaplains to touch a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement explicit handling procedures to avoid desecration: use protective coverings, restrict handling to trained or same-faith personnel where practicable, and update procedures when incidents or near-incidents occur.
